newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: WORLD BANK ENDORSES S.AFRICAN ECONOMIC STRATEGY.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BANK ENDORSES S.AFRICAN ECONOMIC STRATEGY.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn endorsed South Africa's macro-economic plan on Friday and said economic success in the country was crucial for the whole continent.

Wolfensohn, who met Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals, told a news conference afterwards he was concerned about ensuring growth to fight poverty in sub-Saharan Africa.
"We've really got to make a significant move to make an impact on employment, and this is very well pointed out in your GEAR document, which is an exemplary plan," he said.
The GEAR - growth, employment and redistribution - plan aims to achieve six percent growth by the year 2000 and the creation of 400,000 jobs a year by then.
"I have lots of confidence in the minister (Manuel) and the government and the deputy president so I would expect that they would achieve those targets," Wolfensohn said.
"The economic progress seems to me on track... it looks to me as though things are in good shape," he said.
Wolfensohn said he did not think it needed to give aid to South Africa, but the organisation is currently discussing a project relating to industrial renewal and competitiveness.
"There seems to be some interest on both sides, but whether that comes to a loan or not is less relevant," he said.
"What is more important is that we're working together on specific projects and they seem to be fruitful... Lending to South Africa is not really an issue with us," he added.
Wolfensohn said South Africa's size and level of development were among its main economic strengths.
"You have to look at South Africa from two points of view: Both as largest and strongest country in the hemisphere and also as an absolutely critical element in continental development.
"If one were to imagine a failure in growth in South Africa, or some sort of real disaster, this would be tragic for the rest of Africa," Wolfensohn said.
The bank president visited Senegal and Ghana before South Africa and was going on to Mozambique later on Friday.
